title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 155 (Prohibition to obtain more than one Director Identification Number)

content.overview: Section 155 prohibits any individual who has already been allotted a Director Identification Number under section 154 from applying for, obtaining or possessing another Director Identification Number.
content.glance: One person, one DIN — no second application, allotment or possession of another DIN.
content.study: No individual who has already been allotted a Director Identification Number under section 154 shall apply for, obtain or possess another Director Identification Number. Correction of particulars of an existing DIN is not a second allotment. A duplicate application or possession of more than one DIN is a contravention. Current-law framing: identify existing DIN; test any further application or possession; apply the prohibition.

sections.heading: Prohibition
sections.body: An individual who already holds a DIN under s. 154 shall not apply for, obtain or possess another DIN.

sections.heading: One Person, One DIN
sections.body: The statutory design is a single unique identifier per individual across all companies.

sections.heading: Correction Distinguished
sections.body: Updating name, address or other particulars of an existing DIN is not a second allotment and does not breach s. 155.

provisions.title: Prohibition to obtain more than one Director Identification Number

examples.title: Second application blocked
examples.body: A person who already has a DIN applies again under a different identity document. Section 155 prohibits obtaining another DIN.

examples.title: Particulars update
examples.body: A director updates the address on the existing DIN. That is correction, not a second allotment, and is outside the s. 155 prohibition.

hypotheticals.question: May a person hold one DIN for private companies and another for listed companies?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 155 prohibits more than one DIN for any individual, regardless of the types of companies.

distinctions.title: Prohibition on more than one DIN (s. 155) vs allotment (s. 154)

misconceptions.trap: Updating DIN particulars counts as obtaining a second DIN.
misconceptions.correction: Correction of particulars of the same DIN is not a second allotment under s. 155.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 155 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm existing DIN. II. Identify any further application or possession. III. Apply prohibition. IV. Distinguish mere particulars update. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Existing DIN facts; alleged second application/possession; precise relief.

examTips: Apply, obtain or possess — all covered.
